messages:
natalie: FYI customer FinStack reports a big spike in 429s during a nightly batch, says dedicated pool didn't spin up fast enough. Logs show long image pull + attach delays. repro steps and logs below.
mike: can you paste the minimal repro and the pod/controller traces? esp `attach_time_ms` and `image_pull_ms` metrics.
natalie: Repro: run 350 req/s for ~60s to the dedicated route `finstack-prod` (seq len small). They hit headroom and requests queue. Metrics snapshot:
```
scaleup_trigger_count=4
attach_time_ms=98000
image_pull_ms=72000
warmpool_allocated=0
min_replicas=2
```
natalie: Also saw `warmpool_prefetch=false` in the customer config (they're on reserved capacity with large custom model docker image ~1.6GB). I suspect image pull time is dominating scaleup.
tim: interesting — if warmpool is zero, autoscaler must fully provision + pull image per new pod. 72s image pull would explain the latency. any throttling from image registry or node disk I/O?
jess: FinStack says registry is their internal ghcr mirror, sometimes rate-limited during their CI runs. They just rotated their image tag last night.
mike: ok. Two angles: (1) mitigate customer impact now -> enable a warm pool for them / pre-pull image for reserved capacity, or use burst capacity to route to hosted fallback. (2) investigate why warmpool=0 despite min_replicas=2.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout to autoscaler agent v3.2 started at 2025-11-03T09:12:12Z on region-us-west-2.
tim: bump — the canary for autoscaler v3.2 introduced a new aggressor: a policy that evicts warmpool entries after 30m idle for large-image customers. looks like FinStack's pool aged out at 03:40 UTC and wasn't re-populated because their night batch hits sudden spike rather than steady traffic.
natalie: that matches customer timeline. They had low traffic overnight so prefetch wasn't triggered. Still, min_replicas=2 should keep pods ready? why were warm pods 0?
mike: good catch. I see a race: when the control plane reconciles min_replicas it checks node label `dedicated:finstack` capacity. If no node has the image pre-pulled and warmpool eviction happened, the controller defers creating full pods and tries warm-pool-only codepath — but warmpool is empty so it short-circuits. There's a fallback bug: it should create pods immediately but an early return prevents that when image size > 1GB to avoid disk pressure. so nothing created -> attach queue grows -> scale triggers but attach still blocked.
jess: customer is on a paid Dedicated plan; they want immediate mitigation and a postmortem. Ticket escalated to enterprise ops.
mike: immediate mitigation steps I'm doing now:
- turn off warmpool eviction for finstack tenant (set `warmpool.eviction=disabled` for tenant id)
- pre-pull image onto 3 nodes in us-west-2
- add temporary routing to hosted fallback for traffic over 200rps
will post commands when done.

natalie: logs when we saw failed creation attempts:
```
2025-11-03T03:42:11Z controller: reconcile fn=finstack desired=2 warmpool=0 -> skipCreateDueToImageSize
2025-11-03T03:42:11Z attachmgr: queued request id=abcd1234 waiting_for_attach
2025-11-03T03:42:20Z imagepuller: Pulling image ghcr.io/finstack/model:20251102 tag started
2025-11-03T03:43:25Z imagepuller: pulled 1.6GB, avg_speed=27MB/s
```

tim: thanks. I'll open a dedicated PR to remove that early-return and add a disk-pressure check with a safer admission path (create pods with smaller ephemeral limits or use init containers for prefetch). I'll also add an alert that warmpool=0 while min_replicas>0 to catch this earlier.
mike: mitigation done: warmpool eviction disabled for finstack, pre-pull kicked off, added temporary host fallback. customer confirms 429s dropped after ~90s. :thumbsup:
jess: I'll coordinate CS comms and request a follow-up call with FinStack tomorrow. Please include estimated RCA timeline.
ops-bot: ticket#CS-4821 updated: mitigation in place, follow-up required.

natalie: next steps owners:
- tim -> code fix + PR (rfc + test) by EOD
- mike -> verify warm-pool health checks + add alert
- jess -> customer comms + set postmortem expectation

mike: noting a separate followup: add a preflight check during deployments that records image size and warns if >1GB for dedicated customers so operators can opt-in to prefetch.

natalie: thanks all. closing the urgent thread but keeping this open for the postmortem updates.
